title: DriftReport
description: One project-level drift analysis report. Drift is the gap between what the project says and what the project does. A report compares two or more project surfaces (intent, specs, tasks/jobs, ADRs and source code, README and AGENTS, marketing claims, design references, tests, runtime behavior, process rules, schemas, token spend) and emits a triage score with evidence references, per-dimension breakdowns, optional architecture-element scores, and follow-up task suggestions. The Markdown sibling at <reportId>.md is the durable human artifact; this JSON is the additive app contract. Storage lives at <workspace>/logs/drift/<project>/<reportId>.{md,json} and is read through the project organization / Task Access layer. Scoring inputs and weighting are documented in docs/reports/drift-reports.md.

schemaVersion.description: Schema version for this record. Bumped only when a non-additive change forces readers to fork. Additive optional fields keep version 1.

reportId.description: Stable id for this drift report. Prefer ULID or UUID v7 so lexical order matches creation time. Matches the Markdown filename stem on disk.

project.description: Project name as shown in the project organization layer. Matches WatchPaths and ArchitectureModel.project.

createdAt.description: UTC timestamp at which the report was created. Must end in Z.

producer.description: Who wrote the report. Descriptive only; producer kind does not grant any capability. Mirrors AnalysisReport.producer.

kind.description: Manual: user-initiated button click. Scheduled: cron-like cadence configured per project. MetaCycle: orchestrator meta-cycle (Layer 2 1/2). SupportingAgent: a CLI agent invoked for drift analysis. ExternalMonitor: Layer 3 external system review monitor.

participantId.description: Optional Agent Message Bus participant id of the producer. When set, joins this report to the bus's participant graph.

agent.description: Free-form CLI / tool label, e.g. 'claude', 'codex', 'system-review.sh'. Optional descriptor; participantId is the joinable id.

trigger.description: What caused the drift analysis to run. Mirrors producer.kind in the simple case; carried separately so a single producer can fire under multiple trigger reasons.

scope.description: Primary scope for this report. Drift is project-first; Workspace, Task, Run, and TimeWindow scopes are supported for cross-project, per-task, per-run, and time-bounded inspections.

kind.description: Workspace: cross-project drift (uses synthetic project key _workspace on disk). Project: default project-level drift. Task: bound to one job folder. Run: bound to one CLI invocation. TimeWindow: covers a wall-clock window across one or more projects.

taskId.description: Job folder id when scope.kind is Task or Run.

runIndex.description: 1-based run index when scope.kind is Run.

timeWindow.description: Wall-clock window for TimeWindow scope. UTC, ISO-8601.

sourceRefs.description: Documents, folders, reports, or event streams that were included in the analysis. Repository-relative paths or stable refs.

overallScore.description: Triage score across all dimensions. Higher is healthier; lower means more drift risk. Computed from dimension scores and weights documented in docs/reports/drift-reports.md. The score is a triage signal, not a hidden decision engine.

scoreBand.description: Human-facing score band. Derived from overallScore and the worst dimension severity. Healthy >= 85 with no High/Critical; Watch 70-84 or any Warn; Warn 50-69 or any High; Critical < 50 or any Critical; Unknown when sourceCoverage is too low to score (see docs/reports/drift-reports.md).

summary.description: One-sentence verdict shown in the report list. Detail belongs in the Markdown sibling.

parseStatus.description: How the UI should present this report. Structured: both Markdown and a valid JSON sidecar. Unstructured: Markdown only. MalformedJson: Markdown plus a sidecar that failed to parse or validate; the Markdown stays visible and parseError carries the reason.

parseError.description: When parseStatus is MalformedJson, a one-line reason a reviewer can read without re-running the analysis.

tags.description: Optional, free-form labels for filtering: 'pre-update-stable', 'post-batch', 'release-prep'. kebab-case.

dimensions.description: Per-dimension drift state. Every dimension carries score, severity, confidence, source coverage, status, an explanatory summary, evidence references, and the score inputs the analyzer used so a reviewer can drill down to evidence.

type.description: Drift dimension. Intent: stated product goals vs current behavior. Spec: written specifications vs implementation. TaskJob: queued/closed tasks vs job evidence. Architecture: ADRs and architecture model vs source tree. Documentation: README/AGENTS/docs vs current code. Marketing: external claims vs shipped behavior. Design: design references vs screenshots. Test: tests vs documented risk areas. Runtime: runtime logs vs expected behavior. Process: documented process vs how work actually flows. Schema: published schemas vs DTOs. Token: declared budget vs observed token spend.

score.description: Per-dimension triage score. Higher is healthier.

severity.description: Worst current finding severity for this dimension.

confidence.description: Analyzer or model confidence in the dimension assessment, 0..1.

sourceCoverage.description: Fraction of the expected source set that was actually inspected, 0..1. Low coverage downgrades the dimension toward Unknown.

status.description: User or system tracking state for the dimension's current findings. New: surfaced for the first time. Accepted: reviewer acknowledges the drift but is not acting on it now. Ignored: reviewer dismissed; do not re-promote. Tracked: a follow-up task exists. Resolved: confirmed fixed (the next analysis should drop this dimension's findings or downgrade severity).

summary.description: Short explanation of the drift state for this dimension.

evidenceRefs.description: Stable refs (paths, ids, log slices, bus message ids) that explain this dimension's score. Reports cite by id; they do not copy raw bytes.

recommendedActions.description: Human-readable action suggestions specific to this dimension.

scoreInputs.description: Transparent breakdown of the inputs that produced score. Consumers may render this as a tooltip or drill-down panel. The exact weighting is documented in docs/reports/drift-reports.md so the score is reproducible from these inputs.

findingsBySeverity.description: Counts of findings by severity contributing to this dimension.

affectedSurfaces.description: Distinct source surfaces touched by this dimension's findings. Free-form labels, e.g. 'README.md', 'docs/architecture/decisions/adr-archive.md', 'backend/Services/Runner', 'frontend/src/app/components'.

recurrenceCount.description: How many prior drift reports for this project flagged this dimension within the analyzer's lookback window. Higher recurrence pulls the score down.

oldestFindingAgeDays.description: Age in days of the oldest still-unresolved finding in this dimension. Older findings pull the score down.

trackedFindings.description: Findings whose status is Tracked (a follow-up task exists). Tracked findings raise the score relative to the same number of New findings.

totalFindings.description: Total findings considered for this dimension, equal to the sum of findingsBySeverity.

findings.description: Optional itemised findings inside this dimension. Useful when the UI wants a list rather than a single summary. Each finding has its own status so a reviewer can mark one item Tracked while the dimension as a whole stays New.

findingId.description: Stable id for this finding within the report. ULID/UUID v7 recommended.

firstSeenAt.description: When this finding was first observed in any drift report for this project. Drives the age input.

lastSeenAt.description: When this finding was most recently observed.

trackedTaskId.description: Job id of the follow-up task tracking this finding. Set when status is Tracked.

evidenceRefs.description: Stable refs that explain this individual finding.

architectureModel.description: Optional high-level architecture model used for software-to-architecture drift. Intended for a marble-style project view. Hard limit of ten elements keeps the map reviewable. The authoring contract for the source model (Markdown + frontmatter) lives in docs/architecture/model.md and is validated by docs/schemas/architecture-model.schema.json. The block here is the per-report projection: it carries scoring fields keyed by the source model's elementId.

modelId.description: Stable id for the architecture model used by this report. References ArchitectureModel.modelId.

sourceRef.description: Path or id of the source architecture document that defined this model.

elements.description: High-level architecture elements. Hard limit of ten keeps the map reviewable.

elementId.description: Stable id for the architecture element. References ArchitectureModel.elements[].elementId.

label.description: Short display label for the marble.

expectedRole.description: What this element is supposed to own or do.

guidelines.description: Important rules this element should follow.

allowedDependencies.description: Element ids or external systems this element may depend on.

sourceRefs.description: Docs, folders, schemas, tests, runtime streams, or reports used to assess this element.

score.description: Per-element drift score. Higher is healthier.

severity.description: Worst current finding severity for this element.

sourceCoverage.description: Fraction of the expected source set for this element that was inspected, 0..1.

status.description: Tracking state for this element's current drift.

summary.description: Short explanation of this element's drift state.

evidenceRefs.description: Evidence paths or ids that explain this element's score.

followUpTaskSuggestions.description: Element-specific follow-up suggestions. The same creation rules as the report-level followUpTaskSuggestions apply: typed candidates only, never auto-enqueued.

Candidate follow-up tasks that could reduce drift. Suggestions are typed; creation is explicit and goes through the existing task-creation entry point. Until createdJobId is set, the suggestion is a candidate, not a commitment. Source-code edits and steering-doc rewrites are out of scope: a follow-up runs as a normal queued task.

relatedDimension.description: Optional grouping label so the UI can colour or filter suggestions by drift dimension.

targetState.description: Initial state for the queued follow-up. Default 1-preparation; 2-ready is reserved for templated topics with a fixed contract.

createdJobId.description: When the suggestion has been turned into a real queued job, the id of that job.

markdownPath.description: Optional pointer to the Markdown sibling, relative to the workspace root. Consumers normally compute this from reportId; the field exists for the rare case where the Markdown lives under a non-default path.
